Free-tier installs bypass vendor review entirely
name: Grammarly
pros: Genuinely effective on mechanics and clarity
Style guide enforcement at enterprise tier
files: Operates on text in place. Document upload in the web editor.
value: Real-time correction and rewriting wherever text is typed, across browser, desktop, and mobile. Ubiquity is the product: it works everywhere without changing how anyone works.
engine: Proprietary language models, with third-party frontier models behind some generative features.

pricing.includes: Style guide, SSO, admin analytics, data controls

quality: Excellent on mechanics and clarity. Style suggestions can flatten distinctive voice if accepted uncritically.
tagline: Writing assistance almost everyone already has installed, reading almost everything they type.
use_cases: Correctness and tone consistency across all business writing
Enforcing a house style guide across a large team
Non-native English speakers producing publication-quality writing
governance_note: The exposure here is breadth, not depth. A browser extension with permission to read and modify text sees drafts of everything: board material, legal correspondence, HR matters, client data, and anything typed into an internal system. It is frequently installed by individuals on the free tier and so never appears in a vendor review. Two practical controls: manage the extension through browser policy rather than leaving it to individuals, and confirm which tier the organization is actually running, because free and enterprise carry materially different terms.
training_optout: Business and enterprise tiers carry stronger data commitments than the free tier. Verify which applies to the seats actually deployed.
